about: The curation allowlist AND the placement map. Every photo the site ships is pinned to one exact Wikimedia Commons file here (never 'the first search hit'), with its group, the episodes it may illustrate, and the caption printed under it. verify_v2.py refuses any committed photo whose term is not in this file.

campus.file: File:Howard University Washington DC - Founders Library.jpg
campus.caption: Howard University's Founders Library — the research university half of the world Hillman is modelled on.
Spelman College, Atlanta — a women's college and the model for Gilbert Hall's all-women dorm life.
Morehouse College, Atlanta — the men's college across the street from Spelman and Clark Atlanta.
Hampton University, Virginia — founded 1868, one of the campuses the phrase 'Hillman's finest' is drawn from.
Jubilee Hall, Fisk University, Nashville — built 1876 from the Fisk Jubilee Singers' tour money.

campus.file: File:Campus Scene - Tuskegee University Campus - Tuskegee - Alabama - USA (34416930016).jpg
campus.caption: Tuskegee University, Alabama — Booker T. Washington's campus, and the other founding model for Hillman.
Cheyney University, Pennsylvania — founded 1837, the oldest historically Black institution in the United States.

campus.file: File:Carnegie Library at Florida A&M University Tallahassee, Florida.jpg
campus.caption: Florida A&M's Carnegie Library, Tallahassee — an HBCU library built with Carnegie money in 1907.

campus.term: North Carolina A&T State University campus
campus.file: File:NC A&T Students In library in 1915.jpg
campus.caption: North Carolina A&T students in the library, 1915 — the same institution whose students, with Bennett College, sat in at Greensboro in 1960.
White Hall, Bethune-Cookman University, Daytona Beach — founded by Mary McLeod Bethune in 1904.
Prairie View A&M, Texas — the oldest state-supported HBCU in Texas.
Bennett College, Greensboro — a women's college whose students joined the 1960 sit-ins.

campus.file: File:Literary Society Building, Alcorn State University.jpg
campus.caption: Alcorn State University, Mississippi — founded 1871, the oldest public HBCU land-grant campus.

campus.file: File:Xavier University Gateway Arch and Campus, New Orleans.jpg
campus.caption: Xavier University of Louisiana, New Orleans — the country's only historically Black Catholic university.

era.file: File:Corrine Barrett reading in her dormitory room 1908 (3192653106).jpg
era.caption: A student reading in her dormitory room, 1908. Gilbert Hall is this room with the door open.

era.file: File:Panasonic VCR (Front).jpg
era.caption: A VCR. In 1987 this is how a dorm watched a film together, and how Dwayne taped everything.

era.file: File:Static viewed on a cathode ray tube television from close up.jpg
era.caption: Snow on a CRT set — the 1987 dorm television: four channels, no remote, one power struggle.

era.file: File:Marching 100, Florida A&M University.jpg
era.caption: Florida A&M's Marching 100 — the marching band as the loudest institution on a Black campus.

era.file: File:2019 State Fair Classic 23 (GSU Tiger Marching Band).jpg
era.caption: Grambling's Tiger Marching Band at the State Fair Classic in Dallas — a Black-college classic game.

era.file: File:SouthernvsTexasSouthern102823-2.jpg
era.caption: Southern vs Texas Southern at the 2023 Bayou Classic — the football game that is also a family reunion.

era.file: File:PVAMUHomecoming11423^152 - Flickr - 2C2KPhotography.jpg
era.caption: Prairie View A&M homecoming — the ritual the revival's episode 3 turns on.

era.file: File:Hampton University Cheerleading Team.jpg
era.caption: Hampton University cheerleaders — the sideline work that homecoming choreography depends on.

era.file: File:Grubbs Vocational College Library Reading Room (10003712).jpg
era.caption: The library reading room at Grubbs Vocational College, a Black school in Arkansas, 1920s — finals week, both eras.

era.file: File:St. John Hospital adult emergency entrance in Detroit 2026.jpg
era.caption: An emergency entrance. The 1991 HIV episode put a Black hospital ward on prime time; the revival's crisis lands in the same room.

era.file: File:AIDS Quilt at 2012 International AIDS Conference.JPG
era.caption: The NAMES Project AIDS Memorial Quilt — the physical record of the epidemic the original series was the first sitcom to name.

era.file: File:Washington, D.C. Members of the congregation of the Church of God in Christ (LOC).jpg
era.caption: A congregation of the Church of God in Christ, Washington, D.C. — the institution the aunties hold together.

era.file: File:Payphone near Richmond, Virginia, 2024.jpg
era.caption: A payphone. In 1987 the dorm's wall phone was the group's only group chat.

era.file: File:Miss Black America 1977, Claire Ford, at USO show c1978.jpg
era.caption: Miss Black America 1977, Claire Ford — the real pageant circuit the Miss Hillman / Miss Gilbert Hall storyline sits inside.

era.file: File:Balogun Market, Lagos Island.jpg
era.caption: Balogun Market, Lagos Island — Kojo's diaspora argument is about a real place where identity gets negotiated in trade.

era.file: File:South Africa House anti apartheid London 1989.jpg
era.caption: Anti-apartheid pickets outside South Africa House, London, 1989 — the same year the original series ran its divestment story.

era.file: File:Sharpeville massacre.jpg
era.caption: Sharpeville, 21 March 1960 — the massacre that made divestment a campus issue for a generation.

era.file: File:2008 Tornado Damage to Westin Peachtree Plaza Hotel.jpg
era.caption: Tornado damage to the Westin Peachtree Plaza, downtown Atlanta, 2008 — the city the revival shoots in.

era.file: File:FEMA - 31188 - A storm warning siren in Kansas.jpg
era.caption: A storm warning siren. The revival traps its whole cast indoors for one episode; the original used a snowstorm.

era.file: File:Sit-in at Woolworth's lunch counter- Tallahassee, Florida (6941222253).jpg
era.caption: The sit-in at Woolworth's lunch counter, Tallahassee — Florida A&M and FAMU High students, 1960.

era.file: File:Greensboro sit-in lunch counter.jpg
era.caption: The Greensboro lunch counter where NC A&T and Bennett College students sat in, 1960 — the local precedent for student-versus-institution.

era.file: File:KSPC Primary Recording Booth.jpg
era.caption: A college radio booth. Dwayne ran Radio Free Hillman in 1989; the revival's students use the same microphone.

era.file: File:Jackson Street Bridge and Atlanta Night Skyline (Unsplash).jpg
era.caption: Atlanta from the Jackson Street Bridge — the city that became the centre of Black institutional life after the original went off air.

era.file: File:Secretary Blinken Attends Kennedy Center Honors Dinner - 53374121987.jpg
era.caption: A benefit gala dinner. The revival's season ends at one: who pays for the institution, and who says what it is for.

bridge.caption: Debbie Allen directed the 2026 pilot. She directed and choreographed the original, and played Dr. Langhorne.
Jasmine Guy: Whitley Gilbert, 1987–1993 — and a special guest star as Whitley Wayne in 2026.
Kadeem Hardison: Dwayne Wayne, 1987–1993 — and a special guest star as Dwayne Wayne in 2026.
Cree Summer: Freddie Brooks, 1987–1993 — back as a special guest star in 2026.
Glynn Turman: Col. Bradford Taylor, 1987–1993 — back as a recurring cast member in 2026.

bridge.file: File:Jada Pinkett Smith at NY PaleyFest 2014 for Gotham.jpg
bridge.caption: Jada Pinkett Smith: Lena James, 1992–1993 — the revival's Congresswoman Lena James is a callback to her.
Darryl M. Bell: Ron Johnson, 1987–1993 — back as a special guest star in 2026.
